In my professional opinion, using this framework consistently would also have two additional benefits that reinforce its use: an automatic attentional wiring and an increased ability to discern transparency over time. It wouldn’t take but a year for you to start to seek intention and learn from darker text and art with darker borders (sorry again for that limitation, artists). In addition, you would almost certainly get better at identifying shades of transparency. Most children would gain the ability to visually spot the difference between 100 and 95% opacity. It would slightly reshape our brains, a sort of grammatical application of Sapir-Whorf [100]. It would slot right into culture rather neatly.
The Best Security: Game Theory

And as for bad actors? That problem actually solves itself, believe it or not. One of my undergrads was in economics, and I focused as much as possible on game theory (mostly for fun, at the time). The term for what we're going to take advantage of is Zahavian signaling. Creators take on a particular cost by honestly marking some of their output as AI-assisted, but they also gain a more nuanced relationship with their audience along with a sort of permission to use AI when appropriate [101]. Authors can always opt out of this deal by returning to flat 100% text and accepting the baseline level of suspicion on all of the words they write.

Bad actors, by definition, want to appear human. Currently, the ones that are trying to build a reputation are doing so in part by taking advantage of a squishy rule in terms of AI usage: how much is too much? As a bad actor I could always claim with full black text that I used AI for some light editing and didn't really notice that it had rewritten the whole sentence. But I pay a much higher reputational cost if I do this with 100% black text in a document while explicitly using the ghost scale. A larger portion of my audience will correctly have their theory of mind network converge on the idea that there's just no other explanation for my words other than that I have explicitly chosen to lie. In a way, the use of this is self-policing.
So that's bad actors taken care of.
Ghost Alignment

It’s good for authors, it’s good for the brains of readers - it’s even good for AI labs. And speaking directly to the AI labs - please note that if this practice spreads, it would be one of the more effective measures we could implement for preventing model collapse over the long-term [102]. I suspect our current tricks won’t work forever, but maybe I’m wrong.

Furthermore, an adoption of the Ghost Scale can be used to help increase the relative density of human intent in training data, leading to a more effective extraction of intent using this process when we begin to build towards this architecture.

The alignment problem has always been about extracting human intent somehow. Let's outright label the human intent as we begin to mimic the very neural architectures overdesigned to extract it: attacking the alignment problem directly from both ends at the same time.
A Closing Plea
It's handholds for learners (human or ai), an exhale of stress from our brains, space for culture to grow, good for the future, and -
Freedom for creators. Because creators won't need to force themselves to seem performatively human just to get someone to listen.

It stops authors like me from feeling the need to open with a curse, use odd idiosyncratic writing choices like en - dashes instead of em—dashes, and sprinkle in out-of-place memes all for the sake of ensuring that we feel human.

As a species, we must interact more intelligently with emerging AI than we did with social media.
This UX framework is intended to be the tiniest of asks that strikes at the core of the issue before negative repercussions start to emerge.
It’s a simple framework that places the first block on a road towards freedom for authors, connection for readers, and a better future for us all.

Formal Proof and Hypotheses

Abstract: This appendix formalizes aesthetic appreciation as the biological execution of Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL). I trace the mechanistic pipeline of cultural transmission, beginning with data ingestion, where bottom-up aesthetic capture is filtered by top-down precision weighting and the biological firewall of epistemic disgust. I map the hardware of empathy, demonstrating how the Default Mode Network and Cortical Reference Frames run embodied simulations of physical artifacts. Formally defining appreciation via IRL and the Free Energy Principle, I explain how the brain minimizes surprise by updating synaptic weights to align with a creator's hidden reward function. Through the lens of information theory and Kolmogorov complexity, I show how latent diffusion models inherently lack the decision density required for IRL convergence, triggering an autonomic metabolic shutoff. Finally, I apply this biological failure state to machine learning architecture, arguing that Cooperative IRL (CIRL) and Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) must supersede RLHF to achieve genuine AI alignment. Applying this model addresses two major issues: generative AI's friction with the art community (via the Ghost Scale, a cognitive affordance and UX framework for signaling intentionality) and AI alignment [via a proposed shift from Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) toward top-down value capture through Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning (CIRL) informed by world models]. Six empirical hypotheses are proposed to test the framework.
Data Ingestion and Filtration

The human visual system processes aesthetic artifacts through orthogonal cognitive pathways: bottom-up sensory capture and top-down intentionality parsing [103]. Bottom-up attentional capture is driven by stimulus novelty and high-frequency contrast, functioning evolutionarily as an autonomic metabolic honeypot [104]. However, divorced from biological constraints, high physical complexity without a cohesive organizing signal inevitably degrades into Shannon entropy [105]. To resolve this ambient physical data into actionable semantic meaning, the observer's Theory of Mind network must reverse-engineer the creator's hidden behavioral trajectory [106]. This biological intent-extraction operates as a continuous execution of Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL), governed by the imperative to minimize systemic prediction errors under the Free Energy Principle [107].

To accurately model this biological integration, the calculus of appreciation must account for the non-linear metabolic scaling of epistemic trust, the cognitive friction of heuristic parsing, and the continuous phase transitions of the neocortex's energetic boundaries [108]. This framework is formalized in the Intent Extraction Limit:
\Psi = \left[ \frac{1}{1 + e^{-k(\omega - \theta_{E,C}(\kappa))}} \right] \left[ -\ln(1-\kappa) \right] \, D_{KL}(Q(R \mid \tau) \parallel P_0(R))

Appreciation (\Psi) mathematically quantifies the magnitude of the synaptic update driven by Bayesian surprise, quantified as the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the observer's prior expectation of human motivation P_0(R) and the updated posterior extracted from the physical artifact Q(R \mid \tau) [111]. Because biological neural networks chunk information to manage working memory constraints, this integration is bounded by Variational Inference (VI), expressed as the minimization of the KL divergence between the observer's biological prior (a flat entropy distribution representing baseline metabolic constraints) and the updated posterior extracted from the artifact [164].

Cognitive integration is directly catalyzed by the epistemic trust variable \kappa \in [0, 1-\epsilon] [114]. Crucially, the brain's Active Inference mechanisms strictly defend their 20-watt energetic baseline using an autonomic sigmoidal gating function [114] [115] [116]. This gate balances bottom-up sensory precision weighting (\omega) against a dynamic threshold of epistemic disgust (\theta_{E,C}), which scales inversely with the organism's available metabolic reserves (E) and directly tracks the alignment of the artifact with the observer's survival priors (C) [117]. Integration is catalyzed by epistemic trust (\kappa), evaluated under Zahavian signaling constraints based on unforgeable production costs [114]. The logarithmic amplifier -\ln(1 - \kappa) was selected because it captures the empirically observed nonlinear scaling of trust, enforces the biologically necessary constraint that \kappa can never reach 1 (trust is asymptotic, never absolute), and scales the gate in information-theoretic units commensurate with the KL divergence term it modulates. The disgust threshold is formalized as:
\theta_{E,C}(\kappa) = \theta_{\text{base}}(E) + \lambda \cdot D_{KL}(Q(R \mid \tau) \parallel P_c(R))

When processing synthetic media generated by latent diffusion architectures, idiosyncratic deviations mathematically collapse because structural execution is decoupled from a biological motor-policy [118]. While the artifact possesses high Shannon entropy (visual complexity) [105], it lacks the high Kolmogorov complexity (description length) inherent to biological constraint satisfaction [38]. Because the variance is stochastic rather than intentional, the biological prior P_0(R) cannot map the output to a coherent human hidden state, and the algorithmic cognitive load required to model this unconstrained space diverges toward infinity (L(R) \to \infty) [119].
\lim_{\text{synthetic } \tau} \left( L(R) + L(\tau \mid R) \right) = \infty + 0

Within MaxEnt IRL, the probability of an observed trajectory \tau is defined by a Boltzmann distribution P(\tau) = (1/Z) \cdot e^{R(\tau)}, where Z normalizes across the continuous trajectory space. When the observer evaluates synthetic stochastic noise, the probability distribution flattens into maximum entropy - no distinct optimal path exists. Because MaxEnt IRL infers R by identifying the trajectory distribution that best discriminates between observed and counterfactual paths, a flat distribution provides no discriminating information; the reward function is unidentifiable. The biological calculation defaults the extracted reward to zero (R_{inferred} = 0). The brain drops precision weighting of the incoming visual data to near-zero (\omega \to 0), closing the sigmoidal gate (\omega < \theta_{E,C}(\kappa)) and actively down-regulating the processing of uncomputable data to conserve metabolic budget [119]. This instantaneous halt is the Generative Crash.
The Trust Exploit and Biological Model Collapse

A vulnerability appears when an observer encounters a generative artifact lacking extractable intent (R_{inferred} = 0) while believing it to be human (\kappa \to 1). Under the Intent Extraction Limit, absolute epistemic trust mathematically suppresses the epistemic disgust threshold. Neurobiologically, when \kappa \to 1, the DMN activates oxytocinergic pathways that directly inhibit the threat and error-detection responses of the anterior insula and amygdala within the Salience Network [165] [166]. This drives \theta_{E,C} \to 0, holding the sensory gate open despite \omega \to 0. Without the metabolic shutoff, the brain must still resolve the flat partition function. To minimize local Free Energy against infinite uncertainty, it over-fits the noise - fabricating a hallucinated approximate posterior Q_{hallucinated}(R \mid \tau) that diverges from the baseline metabolic prior. The brain hallucinates a non-trivial local minimum (R_{hallucinated}) to satisfy the computational requirement of the open gate, mapping false depth to flat, high-probability token sequences. Integrating R_{hallucinated} creates a compounding problem analogous to model collapse in machine learning [44]: the forced synaptic update overwrites the observer's neural weights with regressive heuristic logic, recursively corrupting kinetic and semantic models over iterative exposure.
Processing the Payload through Empathy

To process the memetic payload of compressed intent, the observer's neocortex must reconstruct the physical and cognitive trajectory of the creator through embodied simulation [120]. This structural empathy relies on the activation of mirror neurons and the Theory of Mind network, which actively map observed physical deviations onto the observer's own viscero-motor and somatosensory architecture [121]. Another source of error correction for the simulation of higher-order concepts is the mirror neuron system simulating internal states (i.e., affective empathy). Bottom-up processing gives error correction through empathy in the simulation of the creation of the artifact, complementing top-down processing via cognitive empathy in the Theory of Mind network. Under the Thousand Brains framework, this parsing is distributed across tens of thousands of independent cortical columns, each generating consensus by anchoring incoming sensory inputs to discrete spatial and motor reference frames [122]. I propose that deep visual processing of a physical artifact necessitates the observer's cortical columns to functionally simulate the kinetic physics required for its execution, effectively translating static visual data into dynamic behavioral trajectories [123]. This spatiotemporal parsing is underpinned by a grid-like code in entorhinal cortex, which provides the allocentric coordinate system enabling cortical columns to anchor each sensory-motor snapshot to a unique position in an abstract cognitive map [158].

This high-fidelity intent-extraction relies heavily on the Default Mode Network (DMN), the neurobiological substrate responsible for self-referential processing and mentalizing [124]. The DMN operates as the primary integration hub for the Theory of Mind, maintaining the cognitive boundary between the self and the simulated 'other' [125]. The Salience Network acts as a plasticity gate, determining whether the Default Mode Network's simulated data is valuable enough to permit synaptic weight updates [159]. Epistemic disgust moderates this process, triggered by a large value misalignment in the converged model. The calculation of value disagreement itself implies simulation, which inherently drives Hebbian learning due to gating imperfections [132]. This forced Hebbian learning - synaptic weight updates occurring during simulation despite the disgust gate - is likely the mechanism for indoctrination and propaganda, and the gating mechanism of disgust that resists these effects is reflected in the first term of the Intent Extraction Limit. Alterations in DMN connectivity, such as those observed in autism spectrum neurodivergence, frequently shift the processing burden from affective, autonomic resonance toward highly structured, rule-based cognitive empathy [126]. Conversely, the induction of hypnotic states demonstrates that selectively decoupling the DMN suppresses the self-referential firewall, temporarily permitting external behavioral telemetry to overwrite predictive models while bypassing epistemic disgust constraints [127]. When processing algorithmically generated media, however, the absolute absence of an underlying human motor trajectory prevents the cortical columns from establishing a valid kinetic reference frame [128]. Without a biological agent to simulate, the DMN fails to engage, stranding the observer in localized, purely visual occipital processing and preventing the systemic integration of the artifact's structural intent [129].
The Calculus of Appreciation

The cognitive resolution of an aesthetic artifact necessitates the biological execution of Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL), wherein the observer mathematically deduces the hidden reward function guiding the creator’s behavioral trajectory [130]. This intent-extraction operates within the Free Energy Principle [131]. The mapping between biological appreciation and MaxEnt IRL is not stipulated as analogy but derived from modeling both observer and creator as active inference agents under the FEP: FEP-optimal agents produce policy distributions satisfying MaxEnt optimality via softmax selection over negative expected free energy, and an observer modeling such an agent faces an inference problem structurally identical to MaxEnt IRL. The observer does not choose to perform IRL; any agent minimizing variational free energy with respect to another agent's hidden preferences will converge on the same computational structure. Upon the successful convergence of the IRL calculation, the observer's neural architecture physically integrates the decoded intentionality by adjusting synaptic weights via Hebbian plasticity [132]. This autonomic realignment of internal generative models effectively syncs the observer's cognitive framework with the creator's latent problem-solving architecture, functioning as a high-fidelity protocol for memetic transmission [133]. I formally define "appreciation" not as a passive aesthetic reception, but as an aggressive metabolic strategy: the active reduction of future prediction errors by internalizing a conspecific's optimized heuristics [134]. Consequently, art acts as a systemic cognitive virus, hijacking the observer's Free Energy minimization imperatives to force a structural, synaptic emulation of a distant, unseen mind [135]. Behavioral evidence supports this: when observers are told an artifact was AI-generated, self-reported aesthetic appreciation drops significantly, even when the artifact is identical [160].
The Effect of Generative AI

When processing synthetic media generated by latent diffusion architectures, the observer's neurocomputational framework encounters a catastrophic convergence failure within its intent-extraction protocols [136]. Unlike biological creators who embed idiosyncratic, high-frequency motor and cognitive friction into their artifacts, generative algorithms execute denoising functions that mathematically minimize structural outliers, forcing a frictionless regression to the statistical mean [137]. Consequently, the resulting visual output is entirely stripped of the kinematic telemetry required for the observer’s cortical reference frames to simulate a cohesive behavioral trajectory [138]. When the Theory of Mind network applies Inverse Reinforcement Learning to these stimuli, the calculation cannot resolve a hidden reward function, as the generating system possesses no underlying biological intentionality to decode [139]. Registering this incomputable matrix, the brain’s Active Inference mechanisms calculate an infinitely expanding cognitive load and trigger a rapid, autonomic deactivation of the mentalizing networks [140]. This epistemic shutoff functions as a critical metabolic defense mechanism, strictly enforced to preserve the neocortex's absolute 20-watt energy budget from being exhausted by the continuous processing of mathematically empty algorithmic noise [141].
A Possible Path to AI Alignment

Current autoregressive and diffusion-based generative architectures optimize for the statistical prediction of low-level sensory data, fundamentally failing to model the latent causal structure of human intentionality [96]. RLHF optimizes a single scalar bound to cognitively fatigued raters prioritizing surface heuristics (e.g., formatting, tone, superficial accuracy) over alignment with higher-order latent values (e.g., helpfulness, honesty, compassion) [161]. To rectify this computational deficit, machine learning paradigms must pivot toward world models such as Google's GENIE [162] and Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) [163], which decouple predictive mechanisms from the generative substrate to operate exclusively within abstract representation spaces. This architectural shift mathematically mirrors the neurobiological functioning of the human Theory of Mind, mandating that the system predict the hidden cognitive state of the agent rather than the discrete physical coordinates of the resulting artifact [75]. The biological IRL transaction maps directly onto the next-token prediction paradigm: the observer predicts the artist's next decision given the inferred reward function, and the prediction error updates synaptic weights exactly as a transformer updates attention heads. Consequently, the prevailing alignment methodology of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) represents a catastrophic vector for cultural misalignment, as it explicitly optimizes for bottom-up aesthetic capture over top-down intentionality parsing [161]. RLHF trains models to manufacture frictionless, high-reward sensory honeypots that successfully hack human approval metrics while remaining structurally devoid of biological empathy [98].

Genuine machine alignment requires abandoning these generative reward-hacking mechanisms in favor of Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning (CIRL) frameworks [53]. Within a CIRL topology, the artificial agent is mathematically constrained by an explicitly hidden human reward function, ensuring the system operates under permanent epistemic uncertainty [53]. This rigid constraint forces the machine to continuously update its probability distributions over human intent, utilizing observed behavioral trajectories and cultural artifacts strictly as evidentiary telemetry [53]. Ultimately, alignment research must pivot from surface-level reward hacking toward the cooperative extraction of humanity's latent reward function - building architectures that reverse-engineer our hidden biological reward functions rather than merely predicting our physical outputs [96].
Proposals for Empirical Verification

To anchor this framework in rigorous scientific utility, the following hypotheses are proposed for empirical verification. They isolate the mechanical failures of IRL convergence and the metabolic impact of the ghost scale UX protocol.
1. The Metabolic Conservation Override (Pupillometry and EEG)
Mechanism: The brain shuts off processing to save its 20-watt budget when the Inverse Reinforcement Learning calculation fails to converge [151].

Hypothesis: Pupillometric dilation and EEG markers of sustained cognitive engagement will demonstrate a measurable autonomic drop within 2–4 seconds of a subject being informed that a viewed artifact is AI-generated, compared to identical artifacts labeled as human-made, reflecting the rapid deactivation of active inference processing rather than a slower aesthetic judgment.

Competing account: The autonomic drop could reflect a simple labeling bias or demand characteristic rather than a genuine metabolic conservation event. To control for this, the experiment must include a sham-label condition (human art mislabeled as AI) and measure physiological markers that are resistant to voluntary control (e.g., pupil diameter, skin conductance). The three-phase design (blind viewing → belief manipulation → reveal) isolates the causal contribution of the intentionality belief from generic label effects.
Failure state: If AI art sustains prolonged cognitive load without causing an autonomic attention drop, the computational overload theory is false.
2. The IRL Convergence Failure (Psychometric)
Mechanism: Generative models are regressions to the statistical mean, devoid of high-frequency idiosyncratic human decisions.

Hypothesis: When tasked with explicitly reverse-engineering the goal of an artwork, subject response variance will be significantly higher, and inter-rater reliability significantly lower, for AI-generated artifacts than for human-generated artifacts [152]. The lack of a true hidden reward function prevents the observer's IRL algorithm from reaching a consensus. The neural discriminant must be sought in top-down networks (mPFC, TPJ) rather than bottom-up visual cortex, predicting that early visual responses will be equivalent while late mentalizing responses will diverge.
Failure state: If inter-rater reliability is equivalent for AI-generated and human-generated artifacts, the IRL convergence failure theory is not supported.
3. The Ghost Scale Titration Test (Psychophysics)
Mechanism: Dropping text opacity acts as a visual affordance that reflexively lowers the observer's metabolic expenditure by signaling low intent-density.

Hypothesis: After training in the scale, reading comprehension fatigue will demonstrate a measurable, dose-dependent relationship with the ghost scale. Reading text at 60 percent opacity will result in significantly lower physiological fatigue than reading full opacity text, because the brain autonomically down-regulates its active inference engines. However, the effect must itself be bifurcated: comprehension accuracy should remain equivalent (subjects still decode the words) while the metabolic investment in deep intent-extraction (measured by effortful mentalizing markers such as mPFC activation) should drop, demonstrating that the ghost scale modulates cognitive effort, not basic legibility.
Failure state: If neither comprehension accuracy nor physiological fatigue differ across opacity levels, the affordance theory is not supported.
4. The Kinetic Degradation Effect (Biomechanics)
Mechanism: If appreciation forces a synaptic update to mirror a creator's physical execution, engaging deeply with non-biological trajectories should corrupt the observer's own motor models [153].

The protocol utilizes explicit instruction rather than deception: expert artists are presented with stimuli restricted to paintings (to invite physical reconstruction) and instructed to actively reverse-engineer and emulate the creator's precise brushstrokes. Immediately following the replication phase, subjects complete an unguided "Free-Draw Transfer Task" from imagination. Data capture relies strictly on stylus accelerometry and digitizer pressure sensitivity, measuring kinematic arrests (micro-stutters and trajectory halts mid-stroke) and velocity variance (abnormal acceleration/deceleration curves and grip pressure spikes).

Hypothesis: Artists tasked with replicating complex AI-generated geometry will demonstrate a measurable loss in their own biomechanical fluidity (tracked via stylus accelerometry) in subsequent free-draw tasks, compared to a control group replicating human-made art. The brain attempts to execute an uncomputable physical action space, temporarily degrading its own kinetic reference frames.

Crucially, the motor-model corruption will persist into the subsequent Free-Draw Transfer Task - the brain's attempt to execute an uncomputable physical action space temporarily degrades its internal kinetic reference frames, resulting in statistically higher velocity variance and kinematic arrests compared to the human-stimulus control group.

Failure state: If the artists replicating AI-generated paintings demonstrate equivalent biomechanical fluidity in the Free-Draw Transfer Task compared to the control group, or if motor degradation does not persist beyond the direct replication phase, the kinetic degradation effect is falsified.
5. The Intent-Quality Dissociation (Alignment Convergence)

Mechanism: High-quality AI-generated text and high-decision-density human text are distinct variables that surface quality metrics cannot distinguish. One contains a resolvable hidden reward function; one does not.

Hypothesis: Reward models trained on high-decision-density human artifacts will show equivalent performance on standard language benchmarks but measurably lower sycophancy rates and higher preference generalization than reward models trained on quality-matched AI-generated corpora [154]. The ghost scale is an intent-structure filter, not a quality filter — a distinction current data cleaning methods cannot capture. To operationalize this, we propose an AI Twin protocol: the same Author produces two corpora under identical prompts — one written entirely by the Author, the other generated and approved by the Author using an LLM. The resulting twin corpora are surface-quality matched but differ in latent decision density. Reward models trained on each corpus are then evaluated on out-of-distribution preference benchmarks. This reframes the ghost scale not as a post-hoc aesthetic label, but as a data-preprocessing specification for alignment-critical training pipelines.
Failure state: If reward model performance is statistically equivalent across corpora matched for quality but not intent-density, decision-density is not a meaningful alignment training variable.
6. The Hypnotic DMN Bypass (Clinical Neuroimaging)
Mechanism: The default mode network acts as the self-referential firewall that triggers epistemic disgust when evaluating unaligned intent.

Hypothesis: If a subject is placed under clinical hypnosis to decouple the DMN, the biological firewall of epistemic disgust will be bypassed [155]. Conclusion

We have successfully engineered silicon to execute the autonomic, fast-thinking reflexes of human automaticity at global scale [156]. True alignment, however, demands that we computationally scale our deepest cognitive adaptation: the architecture of intention-reading driven by empathy. We must cease building models that only predict our physical outputs, and instead build architectures that reverse-engineer our hidden biological reward functions, grounding human continuity in the rigorous, algorithmic enforcement of systemic empathy, and an accompanying kindness.
